Count digits: the numbers 1–9 contribute sum n·1 = 45 digits. Numbers 10–99 each contribute 2n digits.

The sum of n from 10 to m, times 2, plus 45.

Sum of n from 10 to m = m(m+1)/2 − 45. Digits through m (two-digit) = 45 + 2(m(m+1)/2 − 45) = m(m+1) − 45.

For 4501: m(m+1) − 45 ≥ 4501, so m(m+1) ≥ 4546. m=67: 67·68 = 4556 ≥ 4546. m=66: 66·67 = 4422, so digits through 66 = 4377. Number 67 occupies positions 4378 to 4511 (4556 − 45 = 4511). Position 4501 is the offset 4501 − 4377 = 124 within the block of 67s. Each copy has 2 digits; the 124th digit is the even position, so it's the second digit: 7.

For 4052: m(m+1) ≥ 4097. m=63: 63·64 = 4032, digits through 63 = 3987. m=64: 64·65 = 4160, digits through 64 = 4115. So 4052 is in the 64 block, offset 4052 − 3987 = 65, odd, so it's the first digit: 6.

Sum = 7 + 6 = 13.
